topic: PNG LNG third-train (P'nyang) expansion — revived development activity
wiki_text: As of 2025-2026 the long-stalled PNG LNG third-train expansion (a ~2.7 mtpa LNG train fed by the P'nyang gas field, PRL 3) shows renewed development activity. Operator ExxonMobil told the December 2024 PNG Resources & Energy Investment Conference it would bring P'nyang pre-engineering works forward to the April-June 2025 quarter, accelerating the concept-select phase 'years sooner than previously envisaged.' PNG's government signed a fiscal stability agreement for the P'nyang project with the PNG LNG partners in March 2025. A final investment decision is targeted for around 2029, intended to be synchronised after start-up of the Papua LNG export expansion (which is expected to provide ~2 mtpa of gas to PNG LNG). P'nyang ownership: ExxonMobil 49%, Santos 38.5%, JX Nippon 12.5%. GEM currently records this third train as 'cancelled'.

topic: Kumul Petroleum standalone FLNG project (Pandora/Uramu) — distinct from Papua LNG
wiki_text: Kumul Petroleum Holdings (KPHL), PNG's national oil & gas company, is progressing a standalone floating LNG (FLNG) project — PNG's first FLNG — separate from the onshore Papua LNG and PNG LNG plants. It would be located offshore in Gulf Province, fed by the Pandora and Uramu gas fields (Petroleum Retention Licences 47 & 50), with an expected capacity of about 1.5 mtpa. KPHL awarded a pre-FEED contract to China's Wison New Energies on 18 October 2024 (completion expected ~June 2025), with FEED to follow and FID targeted for 2026 or 2027. Kumul held a 100% licence stake and intended to farm down to partners post-study. GEM currently records this as 'Train 5' (1.0 mtpa) of the Papua LNG Terminal, which conflates a standalone offshore FLNG with the onshore Papua LNG complex.
